newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada help wanted index falls two pct in Aug.
newsitem.headline: Canada help wanted index falls two pct in Aug.

text.p: Canada's help wanted index, seasonally adjusted, fell two percent in August to 87 (1991=100) from 89 in July, Statistics Canada said on Thursday.
The index was seven percent below a year ago. Declines were recorded in all regions except for British Columbia.

The help wanted index monitors changes in help wanted advertisements in 20 cities. It reflects the intent of employers in these labor markets to hire new workers. Increases in the index are usually followed by drops in the unemployment rate.
A Reuters survey of economists had forecast a rise in the index to 90 points.
(For more information on this release from Statistics Canada's Labour Division, contact Michael Scrim at 613-951-4090.)
